thread:
acme_integration: Hey — our March 15th invoice shows ~2.3k tokens for a bunch of /chat/stream calls but the dashboard for those calls shows ~1.1k. Looks like we're getting double-billed on stream close. Example request id: req_0x9a1

emma_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the full request id and the timestamps? Were clients disconnecting mid-stream or sending explicit cancel?

acme_integration: req_0x9a1 2026-03-15T22:14:33Z -> 2026-03-15T22:14:37Z. Client does a cancel (CTRL-C) after receiving a partial "stop" token, then connection closes. Logs show an extra finalization event. Pasting sanitized SSE frames below:

acme_integration: ```
SSE: event: message
data: {"tokens":120,"chunk_id":1}

SSE: event: message
data: {"tokens":75,"chunk_id":2}

Client: sends CANCEL header / SIGINT

SSE: event: final
data: {"tokens":5,"final":true}

(conn closed)

SSE: event: final
data: {"tokens":120,"final":true}
```

acme_integration: You can see two "final" events — one small and one large — and the ledger seems to sum both. Dashboard only shows tokens up to chunk 2 + first final (~200) but invoice shows ~320.

matt_sre: Can you confirm whether you're using our client-side "client_cancel" header or just closing the TCP/SSE socket? We had a bug where both the cancel path and the connection-close path call finalize(), and if they race we can emit two final deltas within a short window.

acme_integration: We call the cancel header then immediately close socket. The client library is a custom wrapper around EventSource.

carlos_billing: We're seeing a reconciliation spike tied to invoice INV-2026-03-16-A that matches your acct. Please share the full set of request_ids for the session span and I'll correlate ledger entries.

emma_support: Can you provide repro steps so infra can triage quickly? If you can reproduce locally that's ideal.

acme_integration: Repro steps:
1) Start SSE connection: 
   curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=fast-8k" \
   -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
2) After the stream starts and a couple of chunks arrive, send a client-cancel header (or call our client.cancel()) then close the connection immediately.
3) Observe two 'final' SSE events in the server logs, and final token delta that equals the sum of both finals.

Example quick curl to simulate (pseudo):
```
# open stream in one terminal, then in another:
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
# after first chunks, send: client.cancel: true (via separate request) then close SSE socket immediately
```

matt_sre: Thanks — I can reproduce locally using a patched EventSource that races cancel+close. Filed INF-5623 against the runtime: dedupe-finalize on request_id level. Short-term mitigation: add a 200ms debounce on finalize in client or ensure you wait for the final SSE event before closing. We'll push a hotfix to the runtime to canonicalize finalize emissions.

billing-bot: Ledger reconcile record created: reconcile_id=rec_0472 linked_to=INV-2026-03-16-A request_ids=["req_0x9a1"]

emma_support: We'll provisionally credit the affected amount while infra fixes the issue. Carlos will document the credit.

carlos_billing: Issued credit: 1200 tokens (equivalent) against INV-2026-03-16-A for acme_integration. Credit ref: CR-2026-03-16-71. Should reflect in billing portal within 24h :thumbsup:

acme_integration: Thanks — really appreciate the quick turnaround. Any ETA on the fix hitting hosted?

matt_sre: Hotfix target: 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z UTC rolling deploy to hosted clusters; full patch with tests by 2026-03-18. Will follow up in this thread when deployed.

acme_integration: Great, thanks! :clap:
